title: England set to be one of the first countries to eliminate hepatitis C
summary: England is on track to become one of the first countries to eliminate hepatitis C, a liver-damaging virus, by meeting key public health targets. Over 100,000 people have been treated since 2015, with deaths declining by 36% in the last decade. Initiatives like A&E blood tests, GP registration testing, and free at-home tests have improved diagnosis rates, currently at 84.6% of known cases. The NHS aims to achieve a 65% reduction in hepatitis C-related mortality by 2030, with efforts focused on high-risk groups, including those from specific Eastern European countries or with a history of medical procedures before 1991.
key_points: England has treated 80% of known hepatitis C cases, meeting a key elimination target.
Deaths from hepatitis C have fallen by 36% in the last decade, nearing the 2030 goal of a 65% reduction.
Antiviral tablets can cure over 95% of cases within 8 to 12 weeks.
NHS initiatives, including A&E testing and free at-home kits, have improved diagnosis rates to 84.6%.
High-risk groups, such as individuals from Eastern Europe or those exposed to medical procedures before 1991, are urged to get tested.
The infected blood scandal (1970–1991) remains a significant public health issue, with over 30,000 infected and 3,000 deaths.
